text.tspan: This slope is just the derivative of the average of a log likelihood ratio. We can approximate this
with a quantity commonly used in statistical inference, called the Fisher information rate.
This equivalence is exact in the limit of hard-to-distinguish concentrations. I hope I have
convinced you by now that the larger this quantity is, the more distinguishable concentrations
are, and the faster a decision can be made. In this model, faster binding = faster decisions,
up to the limit allowed by diffusion. Armed with this metric for the quality of decision-
making, we can now quantitatively compare other models of transcription
